quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light will turn red soon.
The light will turn green soon.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light will turn red soon.
questions.explanation: A yellow light warns you that the signal is changing to red. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through it.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up can increase danger by encouraging them to tailgate you at the higher speed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Stop completely, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are stop signs. When you see this sign, stop completely. Check for other traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way.
Change your lane position to be more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position to be more visible.
questions.explanation: When approaching a blind intersection, move to the part of your lane where other drivers can see you best.

questions.question: If bright sunlight makes it hard to see your motorcycle's turn signals, you should:

options.text: Keep using the mechanical turn signals.
Honk your horn to tell other drivers about upcoming turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use hand signals.
questions.explanation: Use hand signals when bright sunlight makes your mechanical signals hard to see. It is very important to tell other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols or words. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that a divided roadway is coming.

questions.question: A motorcycle fits you if:

options.text: Your fingertips barely reach the handlebars when seated.
The seat is one foot higher than your waist when standing next to it.
Your feet comfortably touch the ground when seated.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your feet comfortably touch the ground when seated.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you correctly when you can comfortably reach the ground with your feet while seated. Choose a motorcycle that fits you before riding.

questions.question: The best way to avoid fatigue on a long motorcycle trip is to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Take frequent breaks to rest.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on long trips, limit your riding time each day and take frequent rest breaks. Do not use artificial stimulants because fatigue will hit hard when they wear off.

questions.question: Keeping space between you and other vehicles helps because:

options.text: You can draft off of other vehicles.
You have more time to react to other drivers' movements.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to react to other drivers' movements.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your motorcycle at all times. This gives you more time to see and react to hazards and more room to move safely.

questions.question: You can reduce your chances of an accident by:

options.text: Not using turn signals to avoid distracting other drivers.
Making sure other drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Making sure other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to other drivers, clearly signal your plans, keep space around your bike, and watch ahead for hazards. Always be ready to react to any danger.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.correctAnswerText: Both day and night.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear brightly-colored, reflective clothing while riding at any time.

questions.question: What material should riding gloves be made of?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather.
questions.explanation: Riding gloves should be made of leather or similar durable material. This gives you the best grip and protection.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce fatigue while riding?
questions.correctAnswerText: Take frequent rest breaks.
questions.explanation: Take frequent rest breaks during long rides to reduce fatigue. Caffeine and stimulants can make fatigue worse once they wear off. Wear warm clothing and use a windshield to protect yourself from elements that increase fatigue.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves on rain grooves or bridge gratings, what should you do?

options.text: Zigzag to get other drivers' attention.
Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Keep a steady speed and go straight across grooves or gratings. Zigzagging to stop the weave is more dangerous and forces you out of your lane.

questions.question: What mirror must all motorcycles have?

options.text: A rearview mirror on the left handlebar.
A rearview mirror on the right handlebar.
A rearview mirror only if the rider is under 21.

questions.correctAnswerText: A rearview mirror on the left handlebar.
questions.explanation: Tennessee law requires all motorcycles to have a rearview mirror mounted on the left handlebar in an upright position.

questions.question: What should be your top priority when buying a helmet?
questions.correctAnswerText: How much protection it offers.
questions.explanation: Protection is most important when buying a helmet. Choose a helmet that fits well, fastens securely, and is DOT-approved.

questions.question: If vehicles are on both sides of you, which lane position is best?
questions.correctAnswerText: Center
questions.explanation: There is no lane position that is always safest. Change your position based on road and traffic conditions. When vehicles are on both sides, the center position is usually the safest.

questions.question: Which part of the lane is safest?
questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on the situation.
questions.explanation: No lane position is always safest. Adjust your position based on the situation.

questions.question: How can you make yourself easier to see?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wear brightly-colored clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear brightly-colored clothing to make it easier for other drivers to see you. This works at any time of day.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. It shows specific traffic laws for that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: White lines separate traffic lanes moving in the same direction. What do they indicate?
questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass. A dashed white line means you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: When riding during the day, you should:

options.text: Wear dark clothes since it is light outside.
Wear bright clothes so other motorists can see you better.
Be comfortable, wearing shorts if it is hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothes so other motorists can see you better.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Always wear bright colors when riding so other drivers can see you, even in daylight.

questions.question: When loading saddlebags, you should:

options.text: Load the bags as evenly as possible.
Unevenly distribute weight into the saddlebags.
Place as much weight as possible into one saddlebag.

questions.correctAnswerText: Load the bags as evenly as possible.
questions.explanation: Put equal weight in each saddlebag. If one bag is heavier, the motorcycle will lean to one side.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Ride as fast as you would if riding during the day.
Ride more slowly than you would if riding during the day.
Ride faster than you would if riding during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride more slowly than you would if riding during the day.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night, especially on roads you don't know. Going slower gives you more time to see and avoid hazards when you cannot see as well.

questions.question: When a car is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Not change how you are riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow them to pass.
questions.explanation: Let the tailgater pass. Speeding up will not help—they will just tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: When stopping your motorcycle with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Ride a little faster than you normally would.
Start slowing earlier than you normally would.
Merge into smaller gaps of traffic than you normally would.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing earlier than you normally would.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. The extra weight makes the motorcycle slower to speed up, slow down, and turn. Start slowing earlier, reduce your speed, and look for bigger gaps when turning or merging into traffic.

questions.question: If a rider turns too fast, they may:

options.text: Have increased control of their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Unintentionally leave the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast can cause you to lose control. Your motorcycle may cross into another lane or go off the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell you about road conditions coming up. This sign warns that a stop sign is ahead.

questions.question: When riding during the day, wear:

options.text: Brightly-colored clothing to increase your chances of being seen.
Clothing of any color because other drivers can easily see you in daylight.
Darkly-colored clothing to contrast with the bright sunlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brightly-colored clothing to increase your chances of being seen.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Always wear bright colors to be more visible, even when riding in daylight.

questions.question: Unlike other beverages, alcohol:

options.text: Is absorbed into the bloodstream right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is absorbed into the bloodstream right away.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested like food. It passes directly through the stomach and small intestine into the bloodstream and quickly reaches the brain.
